Region: The western sea-peoples: 'ships of Chittim' (Numbers 24:24; Daniel 11:30); usually identified with Cyprus and the western Mediterranean islands, an identification, not a certainty
History: Chittim, son of Javan, is named in the Table of Nations (Genesis 10:4). Balaam's oracle warns that 'ships shall come from the coast of Chittim' and afflict both Asshur and Eber (Numbers 24:24). Isaiah 23:1 and 23:12 tie Chittim to Tyre's shipping news, Jeremiah 2:10 sends Israel to 'pass over the isles of Chittim' and see, Ezekiel 27:6 brings ivory 'out of the isles of Chittim,' and Daniel 11:30 has 'ships of Chittim' turning back the king of the north. Modern scholarship usually spells the name Kittim.
Culture: Seafarers and traders of the western isles, in Tyre's orbit.
Religion: Nothing distinct is recorded of Chittimite religion.
BibleConnection: Chittim is the Bible's west: the ships that come from beyond the sea in Balaam's oracle, Isaiah's Tyre lament, and Daniel's wars.
KeyScriptures: Numbers 24:24; Isaiah 23:1; Isaiah 23:12; Jeremiah 2:10; Ezekiel 27:6; Daniel 11:30
